evidence: Concrete path: graph observes a session close and queues transcript processing (DESIGN-NOTES.md:241; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:32); the request survives summarizer loss and can be rediscovered (DESIGN-NOTES.md:251,255-258). Before retry, the native transcript is unavailable—a condition the older vision itself allows for recovery, while leaving retention contracts open (HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:37). The saved identity/coverage pointer cannot supply the unreadable input, so the summarizer cannot report truthful processed-through coverage and an output artifact as the approved result requires (DESIGN-NOTES.md:256). Across the four artifacts, no source-retention, source-validity, or unavailable-input disposition closes that request; the request/result and retry details are expressly unfinished (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:34,54; DESIGN-NOTES.md:259). It can therefore remain apparently pending despite being unfulfillable, contradicting the stated visible, repairable operational-progress goal (HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:92-96). This is an acknowledged design gap, not a claim of actual transcript loss or a demand that graph archive transcripts.
